proof.text: Work in the ordinary unbounded category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, with the operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ is finite and commutative by clause 4 of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $C_{a,b}=c_{g^a,g^b}:P_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_aP_b$ for $a,b\geq1$. These are the natural isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. The canonical constant coefficient identification on a composite is the composite identification by [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition], so the comparison applies with exactly the coefficient maps of the item. We write composition of endofunctors in ordinary functional order. The canonical functor associator has identity components: both parenthesizations act by $F(G(H(M)))$ on objects and $F(G(H(u)))$ on morphisms. Thus all reassociations below are interpreted by those specified associators.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence] to $j=g^a$, $h=g^b$, $k=g^c$, all endomorphisms of $X$, with its finite commutative coefficient ring equal to $A$. Its normalized comparisons are exactly the $C$ of step 1. For all positive $a,b,c$ it gives the natural-transformation identity
$$P_a(C_{b,c})\circ C_{a,b+c}=(C_{a,b}P_c)\circ C_{a+b,c}:P_{a+b+c}\longrightarrow P_aP_bP_c.$$
Here $(C_{a,b}P_c)_M=C_{a,b,P_cM}$ and $P_a(C_{b,c})_M=P_a(C_{b,c,M})$. No change of coefficient category or choice of comparison is made.

It constructs natural isomorphisms $d_1=\mathrm{id}_T$, $d_{r+1}=T(d_r)\circ C_{1,r}$ and gives $d_{a+b}=T^a(d_b)\circ(d_aP_b)\circ C_{a,b}$ for all positive $a,b$. Thus its hypotheses hold for exactly the prescribed, normalized comparisons.

It identifies every complete ordered splitting tree, every order of refinement, and every positive multiway partition and reassociation with $d_r$, including the normalized case $r=1$. This is the required independence.

proof.text:
Finally the recursion gives
$$d_{r+1,M}^{-1}=C_{1,r,M}^{-1}\circ T(d_{r,M}^{-1}).$$
Postcompose $T(d_{r,M})$ and use functoriality and the inverse law to obtain
$$d_{r+1,M}^{-1}\circ T(d_{r,M})=C_{1,r,M}^{-1}=b_{r,M}.$$
At $r=1$ this says $d_{2,M}^{-1}=C_{1,1,M}^{-1}$, consistently with $d_1=\mathrm{id}_T$. The argument applies to every object $M$ of the unbounded derived category.

title: Coherence of pullback comparisons for Frobenius powers
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its fixed algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$ and $g=g_\gamma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, as in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Use the ordinary derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and derived pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with constant coefficient sheaves and their canonical inverse-image identifications. Put $P_r=L(g^r)^*$ and $T=P_1$ for $r\geq1$. For every integer $j\geq1$ and positive integers $r_1,\ldots,r_j$ with $r_1+\cdots+r_j=r$, write $g^r=g^{r_1}\circ\cdots\circ g^{r_j}$ and use the canonical derived pullback-composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], with the canonical functor associators, to split the powers repeatedly into $r$ copies of $g$. Normalize the resulting comparison at $r=1$ as the identity. Then the resulting natural isomorphism $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}T^r$ is independent of the order of these splittings and reassociations. If $b_r:T\circ P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{r+1}$ is the inverse of $c_{g,g^r}:P_{r+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}T\circ P_r$, then for every $r\geq1$ and every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$,
$$d_{r+1,M}^{-1}\circ T(d_{r,M})=b_{r,M}.$$
Here $T^1=T$ and $T^{r+1}=T\circ T^r$ specify the parenthesization of the functor powers.
